title: This Bird Gets a Quarter of Its Food by Lying to Meerkats

scenes.text: This bird earns a quarter of its food by lying.
In the Kalahari, the fork-tailed drongo watches meerkats dig up scorpions and grubs.
Then it screams a hawk alarm. The meerkats scatter, and the drongo drops in for the meal.
When they stop believing its own call, it switches to a copy of theirs, the meerkats' own alarm.
It can fake about fifty alarm calls and rotates them so the trick stays fresh.
Up to 23 percent of its daily food is stolen this way. And sometimes, the hawk is real.

description:
A bird that earns up to a quarter of its food by lying to meerkats.
In the Kalahari, the fork-tailed drongo watches meerkats dig up prey, then screams a false alarm. The meerkats dive for cover and the drongo takes the meal. When a victim stops believing one call, the drongo switches to another, including a copy of the meerkats' own alarm; it can fake about 50 different alarm calls. Up to 23 percent of its daily food comes from the trick, and sometimes its warnings are real (Science, 2014).
Which animal is the best liar in nature?

first_comment: Researchers followed 42 wild drongos; in 74 of 151 repeat thefts the bird changed its alarm call so the victim kept believing it. Would you fall for it twice?
